investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node could accept a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885), which requires a kata peer-pod slot that was unavailable, so the probe timed out without producing any evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 124s before the check failed.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the agent never being created.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 147s, no evidence collected.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing peer-pod VMs from prior agent sessions are consuming all available slots, leaving none for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy, so even if general compute were available the pod could not land elsewhere.

Tertiary — peer-pod node pool is under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or user workloads are competing for the same 2 nodes' VM slots simultaneously, the pool may be sized too small for the observed demand.

Lower probability — a stuck or leaked peer-pod VM from a previous eval run that was not cleaned up is holding a slot; the withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) is intended to prevent this, but a prior crash or timeout could have left a VM allocated.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-29T18:01–18:06Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the eval's remote agent pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource are fully exhausted and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never schedules, the agent is never created, and the eval runner never reaches the state-polling logic that would produce the required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the expected-output contract to fail with all four evidence fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production cluster. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource report insufficient capacity (0 allocatable VMs remaining), and the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) from ever completing, so no evidence is written and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence on 2026-06-29 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting zero available nodes due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. Because the pod backing the remote agent VM could not be scheduled, the agent was never created, and the runtime eval never reached the point of collecting any evidence, leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agents workload has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector for remote agent pods. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod request is immediately rejected as Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint in the remote-agent VM scheduling layer, not a code defect in the eval runner or a contract misconfiguration. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the agent pod never starts, so no runtime response is produced and no evidence is collected.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node could accept a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885), which requires a kata peer-pod slot that was unavailable, so the probe timed out without producing any evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 124s before the check failed.
failed-check.timing: status=fail, latencyMs=130612, endedAt=2026-06-29T18:01:09.461Z — the probe ran for ~130s and produced no evidence object (failed-check.evidence: {}).
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the agent never being created.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 141s, no evidence collected.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 147s, no evidence collected.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner invokes createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — a remote machineType requires a kata peer-pod slot.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the VM was never allocated.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: all three remote-agent checks share the same cluster dependency; degradedAfterFailures=1 means the feature is in degraded state after this single run.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing peer-pod VMs from prior agent sessions are consuming all available slots, leaving none for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy, so even if general compute were available the pod could not land elsewhere.

Tertiary — peer-pod node pool is under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or user workloads are competing for the same 2 nodes' VM slots simultaneously, the pool may be sized too small for the observed demand.

Lower probability — a stuck or leaked peer-pod VM from a previous eval run that was not cleaned up is holding a slot; the withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) is intended to prevent this, but a prior crash or timeout could have left a VM allocated.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence on 2026-06-29 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting zero available nodes due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. Because the pod backing the remote agent VM could not be scheduled, the agent was never created, and the runtime eval never reached the point of collecting any evidence, leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agents workload has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector for remote agent pods. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod request is immediately rejected as Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint in the remote-agent VM scheduling layer, not a code defect in the eval runner or a contract misconfiguration. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the agent pod never starts, so no runtime response is produced and no evidence is collected.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 147s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=151241, the pod waited the full scheduler timeout before the check was marked fail, confirming no scheduling ever succeeded.

sibling.remote-agent-create: same Unschedulable / Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message, endedAt=2026-06-29T18:01:09.461Z, latencyMs=130612 — the earliest check in the sequence also failed with the same root cause.
sibling.remote-agent-state: same Unschedulable / Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message, endedAt=2026-06-29T18:03:35.137Z, latencyMs=145676 — the second check in the sequence also failed.
failed-check.evidence: empty object — zero evidence fields were collected, consistent with the agent pod never starting.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, confirming the runtime probe never reached the agent.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the step that triggers pod scheduling; failure here prevents all downstream evidence collection.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false, confirming the severity classification is correct but all three checks share the same scheduling dependency.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all three checks report 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on exactly 2 nodes, indicating the VM slot quota is fully consumed by existing workloads or leaked/stuck pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to pod affinity or node selector rules, reducing the schedulable pool to only the 2 already-exhausted nodes and making capacity recovery impossible without either freeing slots on those 2 nodes or expanding the eligible node pool.

Tertiary — stuck or leaked remote agent pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them: if prior eval runs or user-created agents did not clean up their pods, the resource slots would remain occupied, causing subsequent scheduling attempts to fail.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote-agent demand: the cluster has only 2 nodes capable of running kata peer-pod VMs; if baseline workload already saturates those nodes, any new eval run will fail to schedule.

reproductionSteps.label: Run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Expect the same Unschedulable message if kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agents checks together to confirm shared scheduling failure
reproductionSteps.details: All three should fail with the same Unschedulable message if the root cause is cluster-wide capacity exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 eligible nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Use kubectl to describe the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod affinity/selector and check the Allocatable and Allocated quantities for kata.peerpods.io/vm to confirm exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.label: List all pods currently consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots
reproductionSteps.details: Query the cluster for pods with kata.peerpods.io/vm resource requests to identify any stuck, leaked, or long-running pods that are holding slots.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent pod scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource)
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes scheduler explicitly reports Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 eligible nodes, blocking all remote agent pod creation. This is the earliest violated boundary in the failure chain (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Node affinity / node selector configuration for remote-agent pods
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by pod node affinity/selector rules, reducing the schedulable pool to 2 nodes. If those rules are overly restrictive or the eligible nodes are too few, capacity cannot be recovered by adding generic nodes (failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: remote-agents feature — all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature failed with the same scheduling error, indicating the entire feature's eval coverage is blocked by the infrastructure constraint (source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189).

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner createAgent call for remote agent type
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers the pod scheduling request that fails. No evidence is collected downstream of this call (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918).

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect the 2 kata-eligible nodes for kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion using kubectl describe node; if slots are fully consumed, identify and terminate any stuck or leaked remote agent pods to free capacity.

Audit all pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots to determine if prior eval runs or user-created agents failed to clean up, and enforce cleanup via the withCleanup wrapper visible in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916.

Evaluate whether the node affinity/selector rules that restrict remote agent pods to only 2 of 6 nodes are intentional; if the 4 excluded nodes could be made eligible, the schedulable pool would expand and reduce exhaustion risk.
Consider increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes or adding additional eligible nodes to the cluster to provide headroom for concurrent eval runs and user workloads.

Add a pre-flight check in the remote-agent eval runner that queries available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting pod creation, so the check can emit a more actionable SKIP or WARN status with capacity details rather than waiting for the full scheduler timeout.

Monitor the remote-agents feature status after capacity is restored; given degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 in features.json, two consecutive failures of the required checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) will trigger an outage classification.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval to confirm scheduling is still blocked
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is persistent or was transient at the time of the original run (verifierContext recommendedVerifierProbes).

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Describe the 2 kata-eligible nodes to inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated quantities
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms or refutes the capacity exhaustion hypothesis without requiring a full eval run.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl describe node on each node that matches the remote-agent pod affinity/selector and examine the Extended Resources section for kata.peerpods.io/vm.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the cluster
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether leaked pods from prior eval runs or user workloads are the source of exhaustion.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl get pods -A -o json and filter for containers with resources.requests['kata.peerpods.io/vm'] to identify any stuck or leaked pods holding slots.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run local-agent-runtime eval as a control to isolate the failure to the remote VM path
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If local-agent-runtime passes, the failure is confirmed to be specific to the remote kata peer-pod scheduling path and not a broader agent API or auth regression.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect implicated source paths for any recent changes to remote agent pod spec or affinity rules
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Rules out a code-level change to pod scheduling parameters as a contributing factor (verifierContext recommendedVerifierProbes — inspect implicated source paths).
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Review infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, infra/evals/status/features.json, and infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json for changes to node affinity, resource requests, or agent type configuration.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful remote-agent-create or remote-agent-runtime eval run with collected evidence (orgId, agentId present) would disprove that scheduling is universally blocked.
kubectl describe on the 2 eligible nodes showing available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity would disprove the exhaustion hypothesis and point to a different scheduling constraint.
A scheduler message citing a different reason (e.g., resource limits other than kata.peerpods.io/vm, image pull failure, or network policy) on a subsequent run would indicate a different root cause.
Evidence that the node affinity/selector rules changed recently and now exclude all nodes would shift the primary cause from capacity exhaustion to misconfiguration.

A passing run of the local-agent-create or local-agent-runtime checks (which do not use kata peer-pod VMs) would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote VM scheduling path and not a broader API or auth issue.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-vm-capacity) that queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated ratio on eligible nodes and warns before full exhaustion, enabling proactive alerting before scheduling failures occur.
Add a remote-agent pod cleanup verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote agent pods remain after each eval run cycle, catching resource leaks before they exhaust VM slots.
Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes match the remote-agent pod affinity/selector and have non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, alerting on pool shrinkage.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to emit a structured scheduling-failure evidence key when the pod enters Unschedulable state, so the contract gap (missing orgId, agentId, etc.) is accompanied by a machine-readable reason code for faster triage.
